text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Credit insurer NCM is hit by mass exodus of its directors. (p1)
- Belgium-Dutch bank insurer Fortis signs declaration of intent to take over ABN AMRO Bank's merchant bank MeesPierson. (p1)
- Dealers and other players upbeat over decision to merge Amsterdam Stock Exchange and EOE-Options Exchange. (p1)
- August retail sales up 7.1 percent year-on-year. (p1)
- Dutch state sells its 50 pct stake in property fund KNSF for 7.5 million guilders to General Investment Fund (GIF). (p3)
- Rabobank to help foster South African fruit exports to the Netherlands. (p3)
- Philips Electronics to cut 120 jobs in the U.S. and 145 jobs at its Dutch laboratory NatLab in Eindhoven. (p4)
- Shares in brewer Heineken enjoy brief rally on news that earlier reported setbacks prove less serious than originally thought. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- British architect to take Dutch architect Rem Koolhaas to court over alleged plagiarism in designing Rotterdam's "Kunsthal" museum of contemporary art. (p1)
- Fokker receivers seek talks with standing parliamentary economic affairs committee on future of bankrupt planemaker in event of takeover by Samsung. (p2)
- Eindhoven-based firm Chip Market Europe considers court action against chemicals giant Akzo Nobel for allegedly stealing its idea for super thin solar cells film. (p2)
- Philips Electronics' new chief Cor Boonstra plans to overhaul company's management structure. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Labour considers cutting tax tariff for the highest income band from 60 to 50 pct. (p3)
- Parliament and several organisations question 30 km speed limit in towns. (p4)
- Public prosecutor's office and Dutch banks team up in fight against laundering. (p6)
- Restructuring of automation company Triple P will cost at least 160 jobs. (p13)
TROUW
- Dutch government under pressure to complete revision of Maastricht treaty next year when it holds rotating EU presidency. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Labour and D66 parliamentary parties positive about plans to lower maximum speed in towns to 30 km. (p3)
